_**User**_

You are analysing real UK dashcam accident videos for an insurance-claims demo app called Poodle. Each video will become the 'incident footage' of an insurance claim, and someone will write claim findings with timestamps from your analysis, so accurate facts and precise timestamps matter far more than prose. Never guess: write 'not visible' or give a confidence (0-1) when unsure. The UK drives on the left.

Videos (1920x1080, 29.97 fps, with audio):
- /Users/devansh/hackathonProjects/vast-real-time/poodle/media/raw/accident_009.mp4
- /Users/devansh/hackathonProjects/vast-real-time/poodle/media/raw/accident_010.mp4
Do NOT modify anything inside /Users/devansh/hackathonProjects/vast-real-time (do not register taskboard tasks there either). Write only under /tmp/real/.

Method (you have a shell with ffmpeg/ffprobe, and you can read JPEG images):
1. ffprobe each video's duration.
2. Extract frames at 2 fps (e.g. ffmpeg -i IN -vf "fps=2,scale=640:-2" /tmp/real/frames/NAME/a_%03d.jpg; frame k is at t=(k-1)*0.5 s). To save effort, tile several frames into one contact sheet (ffmpeg tile filter) and keep track of which time each tile is. Find the incident.
3. Around the incident, extract frames at 8-10 fps at higher resolution (scale=1280:-2, use -ss/-to) and look closely so you can time key moments to about 0.1-0.2 s: first sight of the other party, the rule-breaking manoeuvre, the impact (or the closest approach if it is a near miss), vehicles coming to rest, and any post-crash segment (some clips end with phone photos or phone video of the damage or the people).
4. Read burned-in overlays: date, time, speed, GPS, camera brand/model, number plates if legible, and watermarks or banners (e.g. a 'UK Dash Cameras' logo, a 'Submitted by: NAME' badge, text banners) and where each sits in the frame (corner / strip).

Write one JSON file per video to /tmp/real/analysis/NAME.json (the folder exists) with exactly these keys:
{
  "video": "accident_00X.mp4", "duration": 0.0,
  "camera": "e.g. forward-facing car dashcam / motorcycle helmet camera / rear camera",
  "overlays": {"date": null, "time": null, "speed": null, "gps": null, "brand": null, "plates": [], "watermarks": ["text and position"]},
  "setting": {"road": "type, lanes, speed limit if visible", "junction": "none / T-junction on left / roundabout / slip road ...", "light": "", "weather": "", "surface": "dry/wet", "traffic": ""},
  "summary": "two or three plain sentences of what happens",
  "timeline": [{"t": 0.0, "event": ""}],
  "vehicles": [{"id": "camera_vehicle", "desc": "what can be inferred about the recording vehicle", "role": ""}, {"id": "other_1", "desc": "type, colour, make/model if recognisable", "role": "", "first_seen": 0.0}],
  "impact": {"happens": true, "t": null, "type": "e.g. front-to-side / rear-end / sideswipe / near miss", "parts": "which parts of which vehicles touch", "confidence": 0.0},
  "fault": {"party": "camera_vehicle / other_1 / shared / unclear", "reason": "", "highway_code": "rule numbers if confident, e.g. 170-172 emerging from junctions, 185 roundabouts, 133-134 lane changes, 126 following distance, 211-213 motorcyclists, 159-161 moving off, 175 traffic lights, 259 joining a motorway; else null", "confidence": 0.0},
  "damage": [{"t": 0.0, "desc": "visible damage and where"}],
  "post_incident_segment": {"starts": null, "desc": ""},
  "key_frames": {"rule_break": null, "impact": null, "damage": null},
  "notes": "uncertainties, anything odd"
}
Key-frame times must be exact moments (seconds from the start of the file, 2 decimals) where a single frame clearly shows that thing, because object detection will be run on those exact frames.

Final response: for each video give 4-6 lines covering the summary, the impact time, who is at fault and why (with the Highway Code rule if confident), the key-frame times, and anything uncertain. End with the JSON file paths.
